eonet-cyclone-eonet_25290.summary: Hurricane Trudy, which started on 13 October 2026, brought heavy rain, flooding and strong winds to Mexico's Pacific coast. In Colima, 71 homes and 35 businesses were reported damaged, and one death was reported in Guerrero. By 18 October the storm was moving away and weakening, and hurricane watches and warnings had expired by Sunday night. Authorities warned that rain could still cause landslides and flooding.

gdacs-cyclone-tc-1001338.summary: Super Typhoon Champi (Typhoon No. 30) started on 14 October 2026. On 17-18 October it missed Guam narrowly but still affected southern Guam and other islands, tearing off roofs and knocking down trees. Several Northern Mariana Islands communities lost electricity and water, and Red Cross shelters were opened. As of 20 October the storm was forecast to reach violent strength and turn north, possibly near Japan's Ishigaki Island. No effects in Japan have been reported.

gdacs-drought-dr-1018332.summary: Drought in Europe, started 21 December 2025, is ongoing according to the latest sources found. The JRC European Drought Observatory said in mid-September 2026 that conditions stayed stable yet critical across most of Europe. The GDACS alert, last updated 19 October 2026, covers 1,759,971 km² of agricultural drought across 27 countries. Research was cut short, so coverage is partial.

gdacs-drought-dr-1027449.summary: A drought affecting Central America began on 21 April 2026 and is ongoing as of 20 October 2026. Honduras has red alerts in 103 municipalities across eight departments. El Salvador has had a national red alert since 25 August. Guatemala requested a red drought alert for 15 municipalities in the Trifinio Region. Red Cross early action targets more than 22,000 people in El Salvador, Guatemala and Colombia.

gdacs-drought-dr-1027450.summary: Drought began on 21 June 2026 across parts of East Africa and the Central Sahel. The June to September dry season was exceptionally dry in much of northern and western East Africa, with some areas recording their driest season on record. Rainfall deficits have affected parts of Ethiopia and South Sudan. As of 19 October 2026 the event is ongoing, but forecasts for October to December point to above-average rainfall and flood risk in the Horn of Africa.

ifrc-flood-8013.summary: Prolonged heavy monsoon rain from 5 July 2026 caused flooding, flash floods, waterlogging and landslides across Cox's Bazar District, Bangladesh, and other districts in the southeast and northeast. Floodwater was receding across Cox's Bazar by 17 July. As of 12 July, 51 deaths were reported. About 1.11 million people were affected across 10 districts. No current flooding was reported as of 20 October 2026.
